what_this_is: The noticer as a Workshop tool: kept running by its wake, it tells the engine one fact per thing that showed up or went away.

payload.label: Notice when something shows up, and tell the engine
payload.job: Keep watching for things outside (a stretch of time passing, a drive attached or removed, files someone finished putting in a place, a delivery over the network) and tell the person's engine one fact each time, so any tool whose wake hears that kind of fact starts
payload.description: Give waiters: the standing orders the noticer keeps (notice-when-something-shows-up.waiter-descriptor rows, each naming one mechanism in do-work/mechanisms, its settings and the kind of fact it emits). It runs as a kept-open program: while its wake is on, each waiter waits, and each time something shows up or goes away it tells the engine one fact at wake:arrive, of the waiter's kind, with the change's fields as text. A tool hears it by declaring a wake {fact: {kind, from: ["run"], match}}. This row may tell only the kinds its rights name. Each fact told or refused is one line of the program's output. Given for_seconds, it watches that long and answers {told, refused}. A second wake, keep-noticing-row-changes, watches one database's changes (the row-changes leaf) over the connection the person keeps under own-rows-postgres-connection; it is off until the person switches it on, and only then does the run hold that connection and reach its host. A third wake, keep-noticing-one-source, names no waiter and no credential: the person switches it on with their own input (wake:switch input {credential_name, waiters}), so a source of theirs (a booking service's list, their sent mail) is watched from their own DATA and never from a shared row; one source per switch, because a run reaches only the hosts every value it holds may go to.

for_seconds.description: Watch this long, then answer every fact told; left out, it watches until it is stopped (its wake keeps it running).

credential_name.description: The vault name of what the waiters read with, when one credential serves them all, handed to the run on descriptor 4: a database connection a row-changes waiter reads, a key a service-lists waiter asks a service's list with, or a signing secret a signed-service-calls waiter checks calls with. Only that credential's hosts are reached. A waiter that names its own credential_name reads with that one instead, held on descriptor 5 plus its place in waiters, so one run watches many places, each with its own credential.

mechanism_settings.look_again_why: A wake switched on since the last look is watched within a minute; reading the list is one door call a minute.

waiters.why: What timed-action says is due (tools/run-work-later-or-on-a-repeat whenToWake), told as a fact once per occurrence. The schedules are the ones the switched-on wakes that hear due-time ask for in their watch (wake:list), so each lives once, on the row that wants it: a tool hears its own with a wake {fact: {kind: due-time, from: [run], match: {schedule_id}, watch: {schedules: [...]}}}.

mechanism_settings.look_again_why: NOTIFY wakes it at once; the reread catches a notice lost while it was not listening.

waiters.why: Each change of a table the person's AI attached record_row_change() to, in the database whose connection the person names as credential_name when switching this wake on (a vault name they keep, such as the one workflow:make-a-database-for-each-pursuit makes; a shared row names none), told once in commit order. The fact carries the change itself: where (the vault name of what is watched), table_name, op, at, key (the change's own key in that database), and before and after as JSON text when each fits the engine's 1,024 bytes a field (else left out, and a run that needs more reads it by key in the store's own language). No reader tool is needed. This waiter is one way a Postgres database tells its changes; another store tells its own (workflow:tell-me-when-something-changes). A tool hears it with a wake {fact: {kind: row-changes, from: [run], match: {table_name}}}.

A repository's main line moved (GitHub compare API, public repository, no credential). A move is told only when a kind holds: old-code-parked (a park folder took code in or lost code) or old-code-removed (lines or files removed past the thresholds in this row). Thresholds are DATA here so a small edit never wakes a run.
Edge case: replays one real commit (332230b33) through the move rules. Must fire: a parked removal of 603 files.
Edge case: replays one real commit (c73d0050f) through the move rules. Must fire: two files removed with no new home.
Edge case: replays one real commit (ba7a9a848) through the move rules. Must fire: parked removals mixed with additions.
Edge case: replays one real commit (143e155e1) through the move rules. Must not fire: 25 lines, below the threshold.
Edge case: replays one real commit (eac88c676) through the move rules. Must not fire: nothing removed.
Edge case: replays one real commit (f842a28a6) through the move rules. Must not fire: three lines removed.
Edge case: replays one real commit (e74a7d004) through the move rules. Must not fire: a rename that keeps everything.

provenance.source: bitfield-packages packages/notice-when-something-shows-up (moved byte for byte, moved-from.json): its resident emitter and mechanisms, with do-work/tell-the-engine.mjs as the carrier to the engine's wake:arrive in place of the retired runtime's record writes

waiters.why: This row IS the clock. Its projection writes the exact clock-tick record at the exact address and path labels clock-ticker wrote, so every trigger rule matching clock-tick keeps firing with no edit.

What timed-action says is due (tools/run-work-later-or-on-a-repeat whenToWake), told as a fact once per occurrence: its settings are timed-action's own rows (schedules; time_windows and actions). A tool hears a schedule with a wake {fact: {kind: due-time, from: [run], match: {schedule_id}}}, a one-off with match {record_id}.

payload.label: Notice each message on this Mac, and tell the engine
payload.job: Watch the Messages database on the person's own Mac and tell their engine one fact for each iMessage or text message that arrives, is edited or is unsent, the moment Messages writes it, so the workflows that hear messages start. It only reads: it never sends a message.
payload.description: The noticer's program (tell-the-engine.mjs) run on the person's own Mac with one capability, read-messages, which the person grants to this tool and which macOS allows only once the app that runs the engine has Full Disk Access. Its one wake, keep-noticing-one-source, names no waiter: the person switches it on with their own input (wake:switch input {waiters}), naming the imessage-chat-database leaf, so which Messages database is watched and from when (history_since) is their own DATA. Each message is told as a something-changed fact at place message, with the same eight fields every message source tells (where, place, change, at, key, by, after, kinds), so the router and the history keeper take it as they take WhatsApp. A Mac that refuses the database is told once at place access with the setting to change.
